children.subject: xAPI coupon validation and application are case-insensitive, so coupon codes that differ only by case collide
children.question: Is a coupon code case-sensitive when it is validated or applied through the xAPI?
children.body: Coupon validation and application through xAPI are case-insensitive: a code typed in another case applies the same coupon. That means two distinct coupons whose codes differ only by case collide, and the promotion policy picks between them.

children.subject: A pre-checked auto-promotion gift on the cart page silently becomes a zero-price line of the placed order without showing in the cart table, count or subtotal
children.question: Does the "+ Add a gift" section on the cart page add a gift line item to the placed order by default?
children.body: Placing an order with exactly one product added to the cart produced an order containing TWO line items. The cart page shows a "+ Add a gift" panel below the product table offering a printer with its checkbox ALREADY CHECKED on arrival, a disabled quantity of 1, and no price. Nothing else on the cart reflects it: the product table lists one row, the cart badge reads 1, "Subtotal" is the single product's price, and the GA4 view_cart event reports items_count=1. After Place order, createOrderFromCart returns the gift as a second line item with isGift:true, price $0.00 and a discount from promotion "Auto Gift (no coupon)", and the GA4 purchase event reports items_count=2 with the printer at $0.00, qt1, carrying that promotion. The placed-order page likewise renders the printer in its own "+ Add a gift" panel, outside the product table, so the order's product table and subtotal still show only the one purchased product. The panel offers no visible indication that the item is an applied promotion reward rather than an optional add-on. Net effect: a shopper who never interacts with the gift panel still receives an extra order line, and a check that asserts confirmation line items equal cart line items, or an items[] length, sees an extra row it never added. The stored order record shows the gift line is well-formed: quantity 1, price/placedPrice/extendedPrice all 0, taxTotal 0, isGift=true, a discount of 0 from the promotion; it contributes nothing to money, since the order subtotal is the other line alone and the total reconciles without it. The promotion fires every time because it is active, has no coupons, and its condition tree is everyone plus empty catalog and cart conditions with a gift-item reward, so the backend behaviour is correct per the promotion as configured. It is not specific to one order or to configurable products: a gift line was on 11 of the last 12 orders of the store, across three shoppers and both configured and plain carts. The gift IS visible over the API - GraphQL Query.order items{isGift} returns true for it - so a storefront order page that omits it from the product table is choosing to, not missing the data.

children.subject: The payment methods a B2B cart offers are the store's active payment methods from availablePaymentMethods, and the set differs per deployment
children.question: Which payment methods does the storefront offer a signed-in B2B buyer, and where does that list come from?
children.body: Observed on store B2B-store, signed in as an organization buyer with one physical item in the cart. The storefront offered six options: "Bank card (Authorize.Net)", "Bank card (CyberSource)", "Bank card (Datatrans)", "Manual", "Pay with points", "Bank card (Skyflow)". Query.cart.availablePaymentMethods returns exactly those six. Their codes/types/priorities: AuthorizeNetPaymentMethod (PreparedForm, priority 1), CyberSourcePaymentMethod (Standard, 0), DatatransPaymentMethod (Standard, 0), DefaultManualPaymentMethod (Unknown, 1), LoyaltyPaymentMethod (Unknown, 0), SkyflowPaymentMethod (PreparedForm, 0). Behind that, POST /api/payment/search returns 21 rows system-wide across all stores; B2B-store has exactly six rows, all isActive=true, with priorities that match the GraphQL priorities one-for-one. Six distinct method codes exist in the whole system, so B2B-store enables all of them. On a second deployment the same store's cart offers FOUR methods, not six: "Bank card (Authorize.Net)", "Bank card (CyberSource)", "Manual", "Bank card (Skyflow)" - Datatrans and "Pay with points" are absent - so the offered set is per-deployment. Every method row on the observed store is isActive=true, so this does NOT demonstrate that setting isActive=false removes a method from the cart - only that the enabled set and the offered set coincide.

children.subject: Cart payment methods render unselected and ordered alphabetically by method code, not by configured priority
children.question: In what order are payment methods listed at the cart's payment step, and is any of them preselected?
children.body: Payment selection is on the /cart page itself, in a "Payment details" section (alongside "Shipping details"), not on a separate /checkout/payment route. The control is a "Payment method*" dropdown. Nothing is preselected: the control reads "Select a payment method" and no option carries a selected state, and Place order is disabled with "Complete all required information to proceed." until a method is chosen. The list renders in full before any shipping address or delivery method is chosen, so it is not gated on shipping selection. The dropdown renders the methods in exactly the order Query.cart.availablePaymentMethods returns them - the UI does no filtering or re-sorting of its own. That order is not priority: with priorities 1,0,0,1,0,0 the rendered order is neither ascending nor descending by priority. It is alphabetical by method code (AuthorizeNet < CyberSource < Datatrans < DefaultManual < Loyalty < Skyflow). The platform developer guide states that a store's priority setting determines "the order in which the payment methods will be displayed at checkout" - that did not hold here. On a second deployment with a smaller set the order was still alphabetical by code (AuthorizeNet < CyberSource < DefaultManual < Skyflow), so the sort key is not per-deployment. The observation cannot distinguish alphabetical-by-code from registration order that happens to coincide with it.

children.subject: A quoted xAPI products filter term matches the whole value case-insensitively but honours * and ? wildcards inside the quotes
children.question: Does a quoted term in the Query.products filter match exactly, by prefix, or with wildcards?
children.body: In xAPI products(storeId, filter), a quoted term such as code:"ABC-1" or gtin:"<13 digits>" matches the whole value: a strict prefix of an existing product code, without a wildcard, returns 0. A quoted term is not a pure exact match, though: * and ? inside the quotes are honoured as wildcards - gtin:"2945100000*" returned 1 hit, gtin:"*" returned 318 and code:"QA-BC-2945-00?" returned 8 on an Elasticsearch 8 provider, and the same held through the storefront barcode expansion on code, gtin, manufacturerPartNumber and a short-text property. Values are matched case-insensitively on this deployment's search provider. A double quote inside a quoted value can be escaped with a backslash and still matches.

children.subject: The xAPI products filter covers products only by default; variations need an explicit is:variation or is:product,variation scope
children.question: Are variations included when Query.products is filtered by code, gtin or manufacturerPartNumber?
children.body: In xAPI products(storeId, filter) the default scope is products only: a variation is found with is:variation code:"...", and a manufacturerPartNumber held only by a variation is found with is:product,variation manufacturerPartNumber:"..." (1 hit; the parent does not match).
